enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . .KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1100 AM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

 - Dry and warm weather through Thursday, with breezy afternoon 
   winds. Lowland highs in the upper 70s to lower 80s.

 - A strong backdoor cold front is set to arrive Thursday night, 
   bringing gusty winds and much cooler temperatures. High Wind 
   Watch is in effect for Far West Texas and portions of Southwest
   New Mexico. Wind gusts up to 60 mph are possible along 
   mountain west slopes. 

 - Temperatures will be well below normal Friday through the 
   weekend. Lowland zones will struggle to reach 60 degrees Friday
   and Saturday. Freezing temperatures over the Sacramento 
   Mountains may lead to a light wintry mix on Saturday.

 - Mostly cloudy skies behind the cold front, with scattered rain
   showers Friday through Sunday, favoring west Texas.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 AM MDT Tue Oct 13 2026

Today and tomorrow, we remain embedded between an upper level 
trough over the Great Basin and ridge over the Gulf. The moisture 
associated with these patterns remain just to our northwest and 
southeast keeping us in a drier region. Any rainfall amounts 
impacting our area would just scrape Hudspeth County. Otherwise, 
widespread dry, seasonable conditions remain in effect. 
Temperatures east of the Rio Grande run above normal while 
temperatures west of the river run slightly below normal because 
of the two distinct air masses we are currently embedded between.

Main headline for this forecast is a strong backdoor cold front
arriving Thursday night/Friday morning. This will be our first
significant cool air intrusion of the cool season. Strong east
winds and scattered rain showers will accompany it, leading to a
stretch of gloomy, blustery conditions Friday through the
weekend.

Thursday afternoon is when we notice a distinct wind shift as the
upper level trough produces a closed low pressure system 
developing to our west. This will invoke a strong easterly flow 
late Thursday evening and through the day Friday primarily 
impacting the western slopes of our area mountains. Temperature 
advecting out of our northeast with this front will be colder 
resulting in a temperature decrease of 10 to 15 degrees. These 
wind gusts over the Sacs and Bootheel will likely exceed 50 mph 
with sustained winds over 35 mph holding out over Hudspeth and El 
Paso counties through Friday morning. Moving into the weekend, the
western regions of our CWA remain breezy through Saturday 
morning. Southerly moisture advects northward by week's end though
current long range runs are not as pronounced and seem to scrape 
the Gila, eastern Hudspeth, and the Sacs once again. Since this 
moisture is moving into a noticeably cooler area, the possibility 
of a rain/snow mix in the highest elevations cannot be ruled out. 
Widespread lowland rain showers dominate the GFS on Saturday, but 
the EC keeps this moisture confined to the western half of the CWA
during the early hours of our weekend.
